topic.title: Molecular Graph Learning and Chemically Constrained Generation
topic.area: Molecular, Biological, and Quantum Machine Learning
topic.overview: Molecules can be represented as graphs whose atoms and bonds support property prediction, generation, and synthesis planning. These papers investigate graph neural networks, variational generators, molecular grammars, and flow networks. A representative graph autoencoder generates molecules through sequential extension steps and shapes its latent space to favor desired properties.
topic.whyItMatters: A graph can satisfy a model's objective while remaining difficult to synthesize or chemically unhelpful. Chemical constraints, interpretable construction rules, and suitable evaluation criteria help connect statistical generation to practical molecular design.
topic.evolution: Early representatives predict protein function and drug activity from structured features. Later work develops learned molecular graph generators and data-efficient grammars. Recent papers add multimodal foundation models and synthesis-aware rewards, while retrosynthesis benchmarks question whether matching a single recorded answer fairly evaluates an open-ended chemical problem.
openQuestions: How can generation balance novelty, predicted utility, and synthesizability?
What independent evidence should validate chemical-plausibility metrics used to train and evaluate models?

papers.title: Learning Repetition-Invariant Representations for Polymer Informatics
papers.tldr: GRIN learns polymer representations that remain stable across different repeat counts, with theoretical guarantees and improved results on polymer benchmarks.

papers.title: Manipulating 3D Molecules in a Fixed-Dimensional E(3)-Equivariant Latent Space
papers.tldr: MolFLAE supports zero-shot 3D molecule editing through a fixed-dimensional, spatially equivariant latent representation.

papers.title: ModuLM: Enabling Modular and Multimodal Molecular Relational Learning with Large Language Models
papers.tldr: ModuLM supplies interchangeable molecular encoders, interaction layers, and language models to support flexible construction and benchmarking of over 50,000 configurations.

papers.title: Mol-LLaMA: Towards General Understanding of Molecules in Large Molecular Language Model
papers.tldr: Mol-LLaMA combines molecular reasoning data and complementary encoders to support informative explanations of molecular features.

papers.title: MoleBridge: Synthetic Space Projecting with Discrete Markov Bridges
papers.tldr: MoleBridge combines autoregressive generation and discrete Markov-bridge denoising to predict synthesis-pathway notations from molecular graphs.

papers.title: MolVision: Molecular Property Prediction with Vision Language Models
papers.tldr: MolVision finds that combining molecular images and text, especially with targeted adaptation, improves molecular property prediction.

papers.title: Omni-Mol: Multitask Molecular Model for Any-to-any Modalities
papers.tldr: Omni-Mol combines a large molecular instruction dataset with task-adaptive experts, achieving state-of-the-art results on 13 of 16 jointly tuned tasks.

papers.title: Reaction Prediction via Interaction Modeling of Symmetric Difference Shingle Sets
papers.tldr: ReaDISH combines order-invariant molecular encoding with interaction attention to improve reaction prediction and robustness to input reordering.

papers.title: RoFt-Mol: Benchmarking Robust Fine-tuning with Molecular Graph Foundation Models
papers.tldr: RoFt-Mol benchmarks robust molecular-model fine-tuning and combines weight interpolation with ensemble-based methods to improve regression and classification.

papers.title: Self-supervised Blending Structural Context of Visual Molecules for Robust Drug Interaction Prediction
papers.tldr: S²VM learns from blended molecular images to improve drug-interaction prediction, including for drugs with limited or novel interaction data.

papers.title: Towards Multiscale Graph-based Protein Learning with Geometric Secondary Structural Motifs
papers.tldr: A hierarchy of protein motifs and residue-level subgraphs improves graph-model accuracy and efficiency while preserving the framework’s desired expressiveness.

papers.title: TRIDENT: Tri-Modal Molecular Representation Learning with Taxonomic Annotations and Local Correspondence
papers.tldr: TRIDENT aligns molecular structure, text, and functional taxonomy globally and locally, achieving reported state-of-the-art results on 18 downstream tasks.

papers.title: Controllable Molecule Generation via Sparse Representation Editing: An Interpretability-Driven Perspective
papers.tldr: SpaRE edits sparse, chemically meaningful model features to control both local molecular structures and overall properties.

papers.title: DISSOLVR: An Interpretable and Fast Framework for Aqueous and Organic Solubility Prediction
papers.tldr: DISSOLVR uses physically grounded molecular descriptors to combine transparent solubility prediction with strong reported accuracy and out-of-distribution generalization.

papers.title: From Human Labels to Literature: Semi-Supervised Learning of NMR Chemical Shifts at Scale
papers.tldr: Set-based semi-supervised learning turns millions of unassigned literature spectra into useful training data for more accurate NMR shift prediction.

papers.title: GFFMERGE: Efficient Merging of Graph Neural Force Fields and Beyond
papers.tldr: GFFMERGE combines specialized graph models through analytical embedding alignment, approaching joint-training performance with reported speedups of 5–27 times.

papers.title: Learning Adaptive Topology with FiLM-Guided Distillation for Tertiary Structure-Based RNA Design
papers.tldr: ATL-FGD combines adaptive structural graphs with distilled RNA foundation-model knowledge to improve sequence recovery and structural fidelity.

papers.title: Learning Compressed Shape-Aware Molecular Representations for Virtual Screening
papers.tldr: SAND learns compressed molecular descriptors from two-dimensional graphs, enabling reported subsecond shape-similarity searches over ten billion molecules.

papers.title: Learning Molecular Semantic Invariant Representation with Prototype Constraint
papers.tldr: MoSIR learns molecular prototypes and trains for semantic stability under simulated shifts to improve out-of-distribution property prediction.

papers.title: Learning the Neighborhood: Contrast-Free Multimodal Self-Supervised Molecular Graph Pretraining
papers.tldr: C-FREE learns transferable molecular representations by predicting local embeddings across 2D graphs and 3D conformers without contrastive negatives.

papers.title: Order Matters in Retrosynthesis: Structure-aware Generation via Reaction-Center-Guided Discrete Flow Matching
papers.tldr: Reaction-center-first atom ordering helps RetroDiT improve retrosynthesis accuracy while discrete flow matching reduces generation steps.

papers.title: ReCoG: Relational and Compact Context Graph Learning for Few-shot Molecular Property Prediction
papers.tldr: ReCoG combines cross-property relational learning with an information bottleneck to make molecular context more useful for few-shot prediction.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs via Ensemble Consensus
papers.tldr: Ensemble-consensus training uses unlabeled molecular data to improve prediction, robustness, and calibration, with strong gains even for individual ensemble members.

papers.title: SymSpectra: Symmetric Information Bottleneck Framework for Molecular Structure Recognition under Imbalanced Settings
papers.tldr: SymSpectra combines spectral information and functional-group dependencies to improve molecular substructure recognition under class imbalance.

papers.title: Synthesizable Molecular Generation via Soft-constrained GFlowNets with Rich Chemical Priors
papers.tldr: S3-GFN uses chemical priors and contrastive soft regularization to generate high-reward molecules with at least 95% synthesizability in the experiments.

papers.title: When Single Answer Is Not Enough: Rethinking Single-Step Retrosynthesis Benchmarks for LLMs
papers.tldr: ChemCensor evaluates retrosynthesis by chemical plausibility, while the CREED dataset supports training a model that improves under this new benchmark.
